code:
SUCC TWO
= (λn.λf.λx. f (n f x)) (λf.λx. f (f x))
->β λf.λx. f ((λf.λx. f (f x)) f x)
->β λf.λx. f ((λx. f (f x)) x)
->β λf.λx. f (f (f x))
= THREE  OK
description: You can reduce SUCC TWO by substituting the encoded repetition count.

steps.description: SUCC wraps one f around the applications supplied by n. TWO supplies two applications.
Substituting TWO for n leaves its function applied to f and x. The next reduction supplies f to that function.

steps.question: How many applications of f remain after supplying x?

steps.description: The final function applies its argument three times. That is the Church numeral THREE.

title: Add one function application
